blocks.text: Yufan Lu: The Devil is in the Details

Artist Yufan Lu visited over thirty cosmetic surgery clinics in China with her self-portrait, asking consultants to assess her face. Her book Make Me Beautiful uses photography and text to document those encounters.
By Gaia Squarci. Photographs by Yufan Lu

You have a dividing line that splits your face into upper and lower halves,” one consultant tells Yufan Lu. “It brings bad luck to your career and wealth.” The artist turns cosmetic surgery consultations into a study of how beauty standards are sold.

The tone is always matter-of-fact, but no two verdicts are the same. A protruding mouth that needs bone surgery, body fat above the standard, a nose too wide, an asymmetrical chin. One consultant praises her eyes as among the few features that work; another begins by pointing them out as the problem. Celebrities are invoked as benchmarks, and it’s hard not to start scanning one’s own face for flaws.

The pressure is constant. “What do you need to think about? We’ve already analyzed all the pros and cons for you, there’s nothing much left to think about.” Lu’s images bring together her self-portrait, the pre-surgery portraits used by the clinics, and photographs of the clinics themselves, punctuated with classical depictions of beauty from art history and feminine symbols. Their calm, pastel-colored interiors are friendly spaces where self-confidence can be completely shattered.
The book Make Me Beautiful is published by Editorial RM and available at the price of 40 Euro.
